Location: Surrey, BC

Reports To: Sr Mechanical Design Engineer

Salary Range: $160,000 - $195,000 CAD

Position Summary:

The MV (Medium Voltage) Manager is responsible for overseeing the design and standardization of custom, medium voltage (MV) products for the Commercial and Industrial (C&I) markets. This role focuses on streamlining the design process to ensure efficient delivery of designs while maintaining high-quality standards. The MV Manager will ensure that products like switchgear and bus bars meet customer specifications, are compliant with industry standards (UL, IEEE), and are optimized for manufacturability. The role involves global operations and a strong emphasis on delivering custom designs on time.

Key Responsibilities:

Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • Lead the Mechanical Engineering design team supporting MV design.
  • Partner with Maintenance Of Line (MOL) team to assure all designs meet IEM standards and policies.
  • Provide direction in meeting the schedule, dashboard standards, and process consistency across sites.
  • Develop and implement efficient workflows to ensure designs meet customer demands. This includes mentoring, training, and succession planning for the team.

Design Standardization and Efficiency

  • Lead efforts to standardize the design process across multiple locations, focusing on reducing cycle time while maintaining accuracy.
  • Ensure that all designs adhere to relevant UL, IEEE, and ANSI standards, including C37.20 for metal-clad switchgear.
  • Optimize the use of CAD software to streamline the design-to-order process, ensuring designs are ready for fabrication with minimal revisions.

Design Output and Quality

  • Oversee the creation of high-quality designs for custom MV products, such as switchgear (5kV to 38kV).
  • Ensure design output meets customer requirements while complying with safety and regulatory standards, including UL listings.
  • Manage multiple projects simultaneously, ensuring that designs are finalized and delivered to production on schedule.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with the sales and planning teams to translate customer requirements into feasible and manufacturable designs.
  • Collaborate with the production and quality control teams to resolve any design-related issues and ensure seamless handoff from design to fabrication.
  • Provide regular design status updates to ensure alignment with production schedules and customer delivery expectations.

Continuous Improvement and Innovation

  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance the speed and efficiency of the design process, identifying bottlenecks and implementing solutions.
  • Stay up-to-date with advancements in MV technologies and incorporate new methods to improve design efficiency and product performance.
  • Ensure that all team members are trained on the latest design tools and methodologies.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field.
  • Extensive experience in medium voltage design and a solid understanding of relevant standards such as UL and IEEE.
  • 5+ years of demonstrated leadership of cross-functional programs or teams.
  • Demonstrated experience owning operational metrics, dashboards, and reporting for an engineering or manufacturing function.
  • Background in driving cross-functional process improvement, standardization, or governance initiatives.
  • Experience with FEA tools and simulation-based design optimization.

Competencies

Technical Skills

  • Expertise in medium voltage mechanical design, particularly in custom switchgear and bus bars for C&I applications.
  • Strong proficiency in CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks, AutoCAD) and FEA tools for design verification.
  • In-depth knowledge of UL, IEEE, and ANSI standards, particularly related to MV switchgear.

  • Advise leadership on capacity planning, risk mitigation, and tradeoffs among customer requirements, production efficiency, inventory, quality, and cost.
  • Partner with Engineering, Procurement, Quality, Maintenance, and Manufacturing to align operational decisions with business priorities.
  • Perform other duties consistent with the strategic production-planning and operational-analysis scope of the position.

  • 2-4 years of relevant experience required; prior Co-op or internship experience in a manufacturing environment will be highly considered.
  • Demonstrated experience independently analyzing complex operational issues, developing recommendations, and leading cross-functional implementation.
  • Ability to influence operational priorities and make or recommend decisions with meaningful impact on delivery, capacity, inventory, cost, or customer commitments.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office products such as Excel, Teams, and Outlook.
  • Understanding of how an ERP System flows.
  • Proficient verbal and written communication skills. Must be comfortable with organizing discussions across all levels of the organization.
  • Organizational skills, including coordinating tasks, schedules, and resources to keep everything running smoothly.
  • Interpersonal skills such as building rapport with team members, stakeholders, and other departments.
  • Demonstrated career ambition with a track record of growth and increasing responsibility; highly promotable with the potential to take on broader leadership roles within a fast-paced, high-growth organization.

Supervision of Personnel:

  • This position has no direct supervisory responsibility; however, it provides leadership to cross-functional teams by coordinating work, fostering collaboration, and guiding team members toward shared objectives.

title: Production Planner
description:
At IEM, we’re not just building innovative electrical distribution systems, we’re shaping the future. IEM is dedicated to delivering world-class solutions for complex power needs. After 75 years, we continue to push the boundaries of what’s possible. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting out, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, grow, and make a lasting impact on industries that power the world’s most dynamic markets.

At IEM, we’re not just growing – we're thriving! Our rapid expansion means new opportunities are always on the horizon. If you’re someone who gets excited by making an impact through interesting challenges, you’ll feel right at home. IEM is currently seeking a Production Planner for our Jacksonville, FL location, reporting to the Production Planning Manager. The Production Planner is responsible for translating customer demand and forecast requirements into executable production plans that align with material availability and manufacturing capacity. This role focuses on mid- to long-term planning, capacity alignment, and cross-functional coordination to support efficient manufacturing operations and on-time delivery, leveraging ERP tools to drive data-based decisions.

Please note: This position requires 100% in-office presence at our Jacksonville offices and does not offer remote work.

Key Responsibilities

Production Planning & Coordination

  • Develop and maintain production plans based on customer demand, forecast data, material readiness, and manufacturing capacity.
  • Review customer orders and demand signals to validate production requirements and alignment with established lead times.
  • Collaborate with Production, Fabrication, and Engineering teams to ensure production plans are feasible and aligned with available resources.
  • Partner with stakeholders to support resolution of demand changes, material constraints, or capacity limitations.
  • Utilize ERP systems (INFOR preferred) to analyze demand, plan production requirements, and support manufacturing execution.

Capacity & Material Planning

  • Analyze labor, equipment, and material capacity to identify constraints and support informed production planning decisions.
  • Work closely with Supply Chain and Materials Planning to ensure material strategies support production plans.
  • Participate in cross-functional planning meetings to align demand, capacity, and material availability across departments.
  • Support long-range and medium-range capacity planning initiatives.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve planning accuracy, reduce lead times, and enhance overall manufacturing efficiency.
  • Contribute to lean manufacturing initiatives such as Kanban systems, visual management, and standardized planning processes.
  • Support continuous improvement of ERP planning tools, data accuracy, and reporting practices.

Cross-Functional Communication

  • Act as a key planning liaison between production, materials, supply chain, engineering, and customer service teams.
  • Communicate potential capacity, material, or delivery risks to the Production Planning Manager in a timely manner.
  • Support cross-functional alignment when changes occur due to demand shifts, design updates, or supply disruptions.
  • The candidate will be expected to perform additional duties as assigned to support the team and organization

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, or a related field (required).
  • 3–7 years of experience in production planning or manufacturing planning within a manufacturing environment.
  • Experience working with ERP/MRP systems (INFOR preferred).
  • Strong Excel and data analysis skills.
  • Working knowledge of manufacturing processes, lean principles, and capacity planning concepts.
  • Demonstrated career ambition with a track record of growth and increasing responsibility; highly promotable with the potential to take on broader leadership roles within a fast-paced, high-growth organization.
  • Strong communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
  • Collaborative mindset with the ability to work effectively across cross-functional teams.

description:

PURPOSE OF POSITION:

This role leads daily testing and inspection operations, ensures product conformance to UL standards and customer requirements, and supports quality, safety, delivery, and cost goals across all test areas. The supervisor manages test technicians, coordinates priorities with production, and drives consistent process execution across the value stream.

This position will be based temporarily in NE San Antonio while our new manufacturing plant is coming online. Our permanent location is approximately 25 minutes away at Brooks, 7515 Inner Circle Dr., San Antonio, 78235. The position is also 100% in-office and does not offer remote work.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Lead daily activities of Test Technicians and Inspectors supporting various product lines within the site.
  • Align testing and inspection tasks with the production schedule and communicated priorities.
  • Ensure adherence to UL standards, customer specifications, electrical testing requirements, and company policies.
  • Oversee testing processes including hipot, megger, torque checks, functional testing, continuity inspections, and other required verifications.
  • Verify all testing logs, data sheets, inspection forms, and digital entries are accurate and complete.
  • Support root cause investigations and corrective or preventative actions for test or quality issues.
  • Train and mentor team members on test procedures, safety practices, documentation, and equipment usage.
  • Coordinate with Production, Engineering, Project Management, and Materials teams to resolve test failures, part shortages, or missing documentation.
  • Maintain test equipment readiness including calibration, safety checks, and proper storage.
  • Monitor daily performance indicators including first-time quality, test throughput, retest rates, and downtime.
  • Communicate risk conditions, schedule conflicts, and equipment concerns to the Test and Inspection Manager.
  • Support continuous improvement activities through accurate data collection and participation in process reviews.
  • Enforce escalation procedures for safety events, quality issues, and critical equipment failures.
  • Manage workforce expectations related to attendance, conduct, performance, and company policies.
  • Flexible and adaptable team player who operates with agility and resourcefulness and thrives in an often-changing environment. You will be operating with a start-up mindset and must be willing to help wherever needed - "not my job" is an unacceptable response.

SUPERVISION OF PERSONNEL:

  • QC Leads
  • Team Coordinators
  • QC Inspectors
  • Test Technicians

COMPETENCIES:

  1. Safety and Compliance • Safety Awareness, including electrical safety, PPE use, lockout requirements, and safe use of test equipment. • Compliance with UL testing and inspections requirements, standardized test procedures, and inspection checklists. • Consistent application of documented processes across all shifts.
  2. Quality and Technical Expertise • Strong understanding of electrical testing, QC processes, inspection documentation, and test failure analysis. • High attention to detail during inspections, data entry, and test result validation. • Ability to identify nonconformances, support root cause actions, and maintain proper documentation.
  3. Leadership and Teamwork • Clear guidance and direction for technicians and inspectors. • Effective collaboration with cross-functional teams. • Strong communication with test leads, QC leads, and production partners. • Skills in addressing conflict and supporting a positive work environment. • Coaching, mentoring, and supporting team development.
  4. Operational and Problem-Solving Skills Ability to resolve production and testing issues quickly. • Strong prioritization and task organization to maintain testing throughput. • Accountability for schedule adherence, quality performance, and consistent process execution. • Adaptability to shifting priorities or unplanned challenges.
  5. Growth and Development • Support training for new hires and existing team members. • Proactive approach to continuous improvement and professional development. • Commitment to improving test processes, documentation, and safe work practices.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): • Safety: Recordable events, near misses, PPE adherence, test cabinet safety compliance. • Quality: First-time pass rate, test failure accuracy, documentation completeness, rework reduction. • Delivery: On-time testing performance, test throughput, bottleneck reduction. • Cost: Overtime control, reduction in retest hours, calibration readiness, equipment care.

  • At least 2 years of direct supervisory experience with production, engineering, warehouse and quality functions in a manufacturing/plant environment
  • Considerable experience with Measuring and Test Equipment is
  • Advanced proficiency of Microsoft Office applications (Access, Outlook, Excel and PowerPoint)
  • Lean Manufacturing and process improvement preferred
  • Prior experience with ETQ Reliance and/or Infor (Syteline) ERP systems is a plus.
  • Previous experience in manufacturing or production preferred.

title: Senior Business Analyst
description:
At IEM, we’re not just building innovative electrical distribution systems, we’re shaping the future. IEM is dedicated to delivering world-class solutions for complex power needs. After 75 years, we continue to push the boundaries of what’s possible. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting out, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, grow, and make a lasting impact on industries that power the world’s most dynamic markets.

Location: Austin, TX (Hybrid; partially remote with some travel required initially to IEM facilities or for project kickoffs)

Reports To: Director of Solutions Delivery & Operations

Position Summary

IEM is seeking a senior, consultative Business Analyst with strong Salesforce experience to lead business discovery and delivery for enterprise technology initiatives. In this role, you will partner with business leaders, operational teams, developers, and testers to define practical Salesforce-enabled solutions across Sales, Service, Field Service, legal/contract, and related business functions. You will translate business outcomes into a prioritized Agile backlog, connecting epics, user stories, tasks, acceptance criteria, testing, and release readiness across Salesforce, MuleSoft, and AI platforms.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead stakeholder discovery and requirements acquisition: Facilitate interviews, workshops, process walkthroughs, and playback sessions with end users and stakeholders to uncover business goals, pain points, business rules, data needs, and success measures; translate findings into clear, testable requirements
  • Lead stakeholders to decisions and recommended solutions: Guide cross-functional stakeholders through options, tradeoffs, dependencies, and impacts; present practical recommendations that improve Salesforce-enabled processes, data quality, reporting, automation, and user experience
  • Structure and manage Agile work: Translate strategic objectives into epics, decompose epics into features and user stories, and support the team in identifying implementation tasks. Define acceptance criteria, business rules, dependencies, assumptions, and priorities so work is ready for refinement, sprint planning, development, testing, and release
  • Support testing and release readiness: Partner with QA, testers, and business users to define test scenarios, confirm acceptance criteria, coordinate UAT, track and triage issues, and obtain business sign-off for releases
  • Document processes and workflows: Create and maintain current and future-state process maps, standard operating procedures, flow diagrams, data requirements, and technical specifications
  • Develop user enablement materials: Create job aids, quick reference guides, FAQs, and release communications that support adoption of new or updated Salesforce-enabled processes and systems
  • Manage and prioritize the backlog: Maintain traceability from business objectives through epics, user stories, testing, and release. Partner with product owners to prioritize Salesforce, MuleSoft, and AI requirements based on business value, risk, dependencies, and delivery capacity
  • Facilitate Agile delivery: Actively lead or participate in backlog refinement, sprint planning, daily standups, sprint reviews/demos, and retrospectives to sustain alignment, remove ambiguity, and improve delivery outcomes
  • Leverage AI tools for productivity: Use approved generative AI tools to efficiently generate and improve user stories, test cases, documentation, and analysis while applying sound judgment and validation
  • Collaborate cross-functionally: Serve as the bridge between operational users, business leaders, developers, IT leadership, and external stakeholders—translating business needs into clear, executable plans and communicating decisions, risks, and next steps
  • Continuously improve: Identify opportunities to improve Salesforce processes, requirements quality, documentation practices, and team efficiency through sound analysis, stakeholder feedback, and delivery best practices

Required Qualifications

  • Proven senior-level experience: 5+ years in a Business Analyst role, including demonstrated experience leading stakeholder discovery, shaping recommendations, and writing actionable user stories
  • Strong SQL and data-analysis experience: Experience with querying relational databases, validating data quality, defining source-to-target mappings and transformations, and identifying upstream and downstream dependencies across Salesforce and integrated enterprise systems.
  • Agile methodology: Direct experience working in an Agile/Scrum environment with hands-on ownership of backlog refinement, sprint cycles, and the relationship between epics, features, user stories, tasks, acceptance criteria, and releases
  • Requirements documentation: Strong track record of eliciting, analyzing, documenting, validating, and prioritizing business requirements, process flows, business rules, data requirements, and acceptance criteria
  • Agile tools proficiency: Experience creating and managing epics, user stories, backlogs, workflows, and reporting in Jira or similar platforms

Preferred Qualifications

  • Salesforce domain experience: Experience supporting Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Field Service, legal/contract workflows, or comparable business domains. Experience Cloud is a plus
  • MuleSoft and integration experience: Familiarity with integration concepts, APIs, MuleSoft platform capabilities, and the business impacts of system-to-system data flows
  • AI project experience: Experience supporting AI or machine learning initiatives and understanding of AI implementation considerations
  • GenAI fluency: Comfort using approved generative AI tools (such as ChatGPT or Claude) to streamline documentation and analysis
  • Technical documentation tools: Experience with Confluence, Lucidchart, or similar tools for process mapping and documentation
  • Salesforce DevOps familiarity: Awareness of tools like Gearset or similar deployment and change-management platforms

General Competencies

  • Resourceful, neutral solution-oriented facilitation: Proactively investigate business problems by locating the right subject-matter experts, data, system capabilities, documentation, and prior solutions. Guide stakeholders through complex or conflicting needs using thoughtful questions, clear options, and transparent tradeoffs; help the group reach an informed decision while remaining neutral
  • Adaptability: Ability to work across multiple technology domains and learn new platforms quickly
  • Lifelong learner: Passion for continuous learning and embracing emerging technologies
  • Collaboration: Strong interpersonal skills with ability to work effectively across technical and business teams

Communication and Analytical Skills

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills: Confidently lead conversations with operational and frontline teams, explain complex concepts in practical terms, and create an environment where users can articulate needs, concerns, and process realities
  • Detail-oriented: Highly organized with strong documentation skills and attention to detail
  • Active listening: Skilled at asking clarifying questions, validating understanding, and distinguishing stated requests from underlying business needs
  • Consultative facilitator: Skilled at leading discovery workshops across multiple stakeholder groups, surfacing hidden requirements and handoff dependencies, and translating findings into clear, testable, data-centric user stories and acceptance criteria

Work Authorization and Job Location

  • Must be authorized to work in the United States. IEM does not sponsor employment visas for this position, now or in the future
  • Located in Austin, TX
  • Position is planned for a hybrid work environment with work at Austin office and partially remote with some travel required initially to IEM facilities or for project kickoffs

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and benefits package
  • Opportunity to work with cutting-edge Salesforce, MuleSoft, and AI technologies
  • Collaborative and supportive work environment
  • Professional development and training resources

description:
At IEM, we’re not just building innovative electrical distribution systems, we’re shaping the future. IEM is dedicated to delivering world-class solutions for complex power needs. After 75 years, we continue to push the boundaries of what’s possible. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting out, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, grow, and make a lasting impact on industries that power the world’s most dynamic markets.

Position Overview

The Senior Capital Project Manager reports to the Director, Real Estate and Construction, and is responsible for developing, managing, and administering capital projects from early programming to completion and close-out for the Facilities & Workplace (F&W) Department.

This role ensures projects are delivered safely, on time, and within budget while maintaining compliance with building codes, safety regulations, and company standards. In addition, this role will support the Director of Real Estate and Construction in the development of capital governance structure, systems and processes and manage the capital portfolio.

Success in this position requires strong technical acumen, proven project management capabilities, and excellent stakeholder collaboration skills.

This position will be based temporarily in NE San Antonio while our new manufacturing plant is coming online. Our permanent location is approximately 25 minutes away at Brooks, 7515 Inner Circle Dr., San Antonio, 78235. The position is also 100% in-office and does not offer remote work.


Capital Project Management (Primary Job Function):

  • Manage the scope, schedule, budget, and quality of capital projects
  • Responsible for the whole project lifecycle from programming, planning, design, procurement, construction, integration, commissioning, and closeout
  • Understands the business need for each project and makes on-going decisions based on what's best for the organization
  • Develop and maintain the project execution plan, specs, and documents for capital projects
  • Work closely with the project teams to ensure that all deliverables are compliant with IEM’s standards
  • Acts as liaison with internal and external stakeholders for capital projects
  • Provide oversight and directives for internal project team members and external vendors/contractors throughout the project
  • Manage coordination and communications with all parties involved, including internal and external stakeholders, other agency departments, consultants, and contractors
  • Collaborate with key stakeholders and build consensus and drive decisions and progress

description:

At IEM, we’re not just growing – we're thriving! Our rapid expansion means new opportunities are always on the horizon. If you’re someone who gets excited by making an impact through interesting challenges, you’ll feel right at home.

Purpose of the Position:

IEM is currently seeking a Senior Continuous Improvement Engineer for our Surrey, B.C. locations and will report to our Continuous Improvement manager. Join our transformation journey as a lean professional supporting kaizen activities, standard work documentation, and data-driven process improvement. This is a hands-on role ideal for candidates with a passion for lean manufacturing and a desire to grow in a structured CI environment.

Please note: This position requires 100% in-office presence in our Surrey offices and does not offer remote work.

Key Responsibilities:

Lead Operational Transformation

  • Schedule, plan, and facilitate kaizen events: line balancing, standard work, Daily Management setup, SMED, 5S, visual management, error-proofing
  • Conduct value stream mapping and process analysis; develop data-driven improvement roadmaps
  • Design standard work from the ground up: work sequences, takt time, operator training, visual controls
  • Establish and audit Daily Management systems; coach leaders on sustainment
  • Identify systemic barriers to improvement (design gaps, training deficits, leadership behavior) and address them

Drive Root-Cause Problem Solving

  • Lead systematic problem-solving using PDCA, A3, and 8D methodologies; use data to find real root causes
  • Analyze production data (cycle time, downtime, quality, labor) to set priorities and measure results
  • Work cross-functionally (Ops, Process Engineering, Supply Chain) to implement solutions that stick
  • Track sustainability metrics; conduct post-kaizen audits and investigate deterioration

Build Capability & Culture

  • Mentor E2 engineers on CI methodologies, kaizen facilitation, and systematic thinking
  • Coach operations leaders and supervisors on Daily Management discipline and lean problem-solving
  • Document and standardize best practices; share learnings across teams
  • Develop and deliver CI training to operations, manufacturing engineering, and leadership

Measure & Sustain Impact

  • Own improvement roadmap execution; track schedule, budget, and impact metrics
  • Establish and monitor KPIs: productivity, quality, lead time, cost savings, safety
  • Present progress in operations reviews and escalate barriers.
  • Manufacturing floor presence required; spend significant time observing, coaching, facilitating.

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in industrial engineering, business, operations, or related field.
  • 7–10+ years in manufacturing, operations, or continuous improvement
  • Led 10+ kaizen events from concept to sustained implementation
  • Proven success implementing and sustaining Daily Management systems
  • Demonstrated ability to move production lines from batch toward flow

Technical Skills

  • Deep understanding of Lean Manufacturing: value stream mapping, takt time, line balancing, pull systems, standard work, visual management, 5S.
  • Proficiency in process improvement methodologies: PDCA, A3 problem solving, 8D, root-cause analysis (5-why), SMED.
  • Data-driven mindset: comfortable analyzing production metrics, cycle time studies, bottleneck analysis, process capability.
  • Experience documenting processes and creating visual standards that operators can follow.

Leadership & Mindset

  • Excellent facilitation and coaching skills; you make others better at problem-solving
  • Ability to work cross-functionally (Ops, ME, Supply Chain, Quality) without friction
  • Can navigate disagreement and push back when people want quick fixes instead of root causes
  • Strong communication: can explain complex problems clearly to frontline workers and executives
  • Detail-oriented; you follow through and hold teams accountable
  • Comfort in dynamic, multi-tasking environments; you prioritize and adapt as business needs change
  • Energizing presence; you build trust and rapport across all levels

  • Lean Expertise: You can run any type of kaizen; you understand how tools like SMED, 5S, standard work, and visual management connect.

  • Facilitation: You can draw out the best ideas from a room full of people with different perspectives.
  • Coaching & Development: You invest in people; your team members grow in capability under your mentorship.
  • Influence Without Authority: You can move things without a formal decision; you build alignment through respect.
  • Grit: Improvements are hard; you push through obstacles, learn from setbacks, and keep going.

Success Criteria

  • Lead 4–6 major Kaizen initiatives/year.
  • Champion Daily Management

LOCATION & LOGISTICS

description:

Location: San Antonio, TX

Reports To: Director of Talent Development

Salary Range: $150,000-$180,000

Position Summary:

We are seeking a Senior Learning Program Manager to join IEM's Talent Development team, supporting the launch and workforce ramp-up of a new manufacturing facility. This is a build-from-scratch role owning end-to-end workforce capability – onboarding, internal training, and community workforce development – including leading and growing a team of Manufacturing Training Specialists and standing up switchgear-specific technical training capability.

The Senior Learning Program Manager partners with business stakeholders to identify capability needs, design effective learning solutions, and manage program execution from start to finish, ensuring learning initiatives are well-designed, operationally sound, and aligned to the populations and functions they support. A key part of the role is building external partnerships with local workforce development boards, community organizations, and junior/community colleges to create talent pipelines that support hiring for the new facility.

The ideal candidate brings solid experience in learning program management, strong project coordination skills, and the ability to translate business needs into practical learning solutions. They are comfortable managing multiple workstreams, collaborating with subject matter experts, facilitating learning experiences for a defined audience, and building relationships with external workforce partners. Experience launching training functions in a new or growing manufacturing site is highly valued, along with the interpersonal skill to build trust and credibility with audiences ranging from frontline production employees to senior leadership.

Key Responsibilities:

Manufacturing Development

  • Design, implement, and manage training programs that build technical and operational skills for production employees, ensuring workers are equipped to perform safely, accurately, and efficiently.
  • Ensure all training programs meet applicable regulatory, safety, and compliance requirements, and maintain accurate records of completed training in the LMS.
  • Partner with site leadership, operations managers, and SMEs to develop job-specific learning pathways and performance support tools for frontline and production employees.
  • Design and manage new hire onboarding and ramp-up programs tailored to production roles, including scalable models that support high volume, rapid hiring for a new facility launch, enabling employees to reach proficiency quickly.
  • Continuously assess the effectiveness of manufacturing training and drive improvements based on performance data, audit findings, and operational feedback.
  • Establish competency verification and certification standards for safety- and quality-critical production tasks, requiring demonstrated proficiency — not just course completion — with authority to withhold certification until competency is met.
  • Maintain skill/cross-training matrices tracking employee competency by role.

Team Leadership

  • Build, lead, and develop a team of Manufacturing Training Specialists including hiring, coaching, performance management, and career development.
  • Plan team structure, staffing, and capacity (trainer-to-learner ratios, shift coverage) to keep pace with a hiring ramp of 3,000+ employees over the next two years.
  • Build trust and credibility across the organization, from frontline production employees to site and senior leadership, serving as a key connector between Talent Development, Operations, Safety, Quality, and HR.

Workforce Pipeline & Community Partnerships

  • Build and manage relationships with local workforce development commissions/boards, economic development organizations, and junior/community colleges to establish talent pipelines for the new facility.
  • Design and implement community-based training and pre-employment programs (e.g., pre-apprenticeships, bootcamps, certificate pathways) with external institutions to prepare candidates for production roles.
  • Track and report pipeline outcomes (candidate flow, hire rates, retention) with Talent Acquisition and the site HR Manager to guide continued investment in community partnerships.
  • Serve as IEM’s primary contact for San Antonio-area workforce partners funding and supporting this ramp-up and manage related reporting to the State of Texas and City of San Antonio.

Organizational Development & Learning Support

  • Partner with business stakeholders within assigned functions to identify capability gaps and development needs.
  • Support organizational initiatives by designing learning content that aligns with business goals and reinforces new behaviors, processes, and ways of working.
  • Collaborate with business partners and function leads to ensure programs align with team and business priorities.

Program Management & Execution

  • Lead end-to-end management of concurrent learning programs aligned with talent development priorities.
  • Manage program roadmaps, timelines, logistics, and cross-functional coordination to ensure successful delivery.
  • Execute within established enterprise learning frameworks and standards.
  • Continuously refine programs based on learner feedback, business needs, and performance outcomes.

Needs Assessment & Solution Design

  • Conduct stakeholder interviews, needs assessments, and performance analyses to identify skill gaps within assigned populations.
  • Translate business challenges into targeted learning solutions using adult learning principles and instructional design methodologies.
  • Partner with subject matter experts to develop learning journeys for IC and manager-level employees.
  • Develop learning assets including digital learning, instructor-led programs, and blended learning formats.

Facilitation & Delivery

  • Deliver and facilitate select learning programs, workshops, and training sessions for defined employee populations, including bilingual (English/Spanish) delivery where needed, to support a diverse production workforce.
  • Leverage multiple learning modalities including virtual, classroom, digital, and blended formats.
  • Ensure learning experiences are engaging, practical, and aligned with adult learning best practices.

Measurement & Continuous Improvement

  • Define and track success metrics for learning programs using learner feedback and business data.
  • Track workforce-ramp KPIs, including time-to-competency/time-to-productivity, certification pass rates, retraining rates, retention, and internal promotion rate.
  • Use insights to refine program design and improve learning effectiveness over time.
  • Support reporting on learning activity and program outcomes within assigned functions.

Learning Technology

  • Leverage the LMS and learning technologies to manage program enrollment, content delivery, and reporting.
  • Partner with HR and technology teams to optimize platform usage and digital learning delivery.

  • 2+ years of experience directly managing, coaching, and developing a team of trainers or training specialists required.
  • Experience directly managing, coaching, and developing a team of trainers or training specialists required.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and managing learning programs within a defined function or employee population, ideally within a manufacturing or industrial environment.
  • Experience building and managing partnerships with local workforce development commissions/boards, community organizations, and/or junior/community colleges to create hiring and training pipelines.
  • Experience supporting a new facility launch, plant startup, or large-scale/rapid hiring initiative strongly preferred.
  • Experience in the power distribution or switchgear manufacturing industry strongly preferred.
  • Strong understanding of shopfloor processes and operational requirements.
  • Strong project and program management skills; able to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously with attention to detail.
  • Solid stakeholder management and communication skills; comfortable partnering with managers, senior-level business leaders, and external community / workforce partners.

The Senior Manufacturing Engineer is a key technical leader responsible for driving strategic initiatives and delivering robust, scalable, and cost-effective manufacturing solutions. This role oversees the development, optimization, and support of advanced manufacturing processes, with a focus on operational excellence, automation, and continuous improvement. The Senior Engineer will lead cross-functional efforts to implement cutting-edge technologies, ensure regulatory compliance, and achieve world-class performance in quality, safety, and throughput. This position demands deep expertise in Lean, Six Sigma, process validation, and smart manufacturing systems, as well as strong leadership and mentoring capabilities.

This position will be based temporarily in NE San Antonio while our new manufacturing plant is coming online. Our permanent location is approximately 25 minutes away at Brooks, 7515 Inner Circle Dr., San Antonio, 78235. The position is also 100% in-office and does not offer remote work.

Location: San Antonio, TX

Reports To: VP of Design Engineering

Position Summary:

The Skidding/E-House Engineering Manager leads the structural engineering discipline supporting the design and fabrication of skid-mounted equipment packages and electrical houses (E-Houses). This role is the primary technical authority for IBC code compliance, state licensing, state certifications/inspections, PE stamping, and lift calculations, and manages a team of engineers to ensure all skid and E-House structural designs are safe, code-compliant, and delivered on schedule. This position reports directly to the VP of Engineering.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the primary technical authority on International Building Code (IBC) compliance for all skid-mounted equipment packages and electrical house (E-House) structural designs.
  • Review, approve, and PE-stamp structural calculations, drawings, and specifications for skids and E-Houses in accordance with applicable codes and state requirements.
  • Perform and oversee lift calculations and rigging plans to ensure the safe lifting, transport, and installation of skids and E-Houses.
  • Manage state professional licensing for the engineering group, ensuring the team holds and maintains the licenses required in every state where projects are executed.
  • Coordinate state certifications, inspections, and permitting activities for skid and E-House projects, acting as the primary liaison with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs) and third-party inspectors.
  • Lead, mentor, and develop a team of structural and design engineers supporting skidding and E-House programs.
  • Partner with the VP of Engineering to establish structural engineering standards, design practices, and quality control processes for skids and E-Houses.
  • Review project scopes and customer specifications early in the proposal and design phases to identify structural, code, and licensing requirements.
  • Collaborate with project management, manufacturing, and quality teams to ensure structural designs are manufacturable, code-compliant, and delivered on schedule.
  • Evaluate site-specific loading conditions (seismic, wind, snow, transportation) and ensure designs are engineered accordingly.
  • Support proposal and estimating efforts with structural engineering scope reviews, risk assessments, and man-hour estimates.
  • Stay current on changes to the IBC, state building codes, and state licensing/certification requirements, and update internal engineering standards accordingly.
  • Lead root cause investigations and corrective actions for structural or code-compliance issues identified during design, fabrication, or in the field.

Competencies:

  • In-depth knowledge of the International Building Code (IBC) and applicable state/local building codes as they apply to the structural design of skids and E-Houses.
  • Active Professional Engineer (PE) license, with demonstrated ability to stamp structural calculations and drawings.
  • Working knowledge of state licensing, certification, and inspection processes for structural equipment and prefabricated structures.
  • Proficiency in performing and reviewing lift calculations and rigging/transportation plans.
  • Strong background in structural analysis and design, including relevant structural design software.
  • Leadership and people-management skills, with the ability to build, mentor, and develop an engineering team.
  • Task management and the ability to carry a plan to completion across a number of concurrent projects.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills.
  • Ability to interact directly with customers, sales, inspectors, other technical resources, and management.
  • Technical writing skills.
  • Organization skills.
  • Excellent working knowledge of MS Office Suites (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project, etc.).
  • Pride in workmanship.
  • Manages multiple tasks and deadlines with minimal supervision; demonstrates consistent prioritization and planning.
  • Attention to detail and thoroughness.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Structural, Civil, or Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent professional experience.
  • 15+ years of structural engineering experience within the skidding/E-House industry.
  • Active Professional Engineer (PE) license required; ability to obtain licensure/reciprocity in additional states as needed.
  • Demonstrated experience with IBC compliance, state licensing, state certifications/inspections, PE stamping, and lift calculations.
  • Prior experience managing or leading an engineering team preferred.
  • Experience working directly with customers, third-party inspectors, and Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs) preferred.

Position Summary:

The Supply Planning Manager is responsible for owning and driving the enterprise supply plan, including rough-cut capacity planning, as a core component of the company's Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) cycle. This role serves as the primary liaison between the supply chain organization and plant Operations, ensuring supply plans are feasible, executable, and aligned to customer demand.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and maintain the enterprise supply plan, translating the consensus demand plan into a feasible production and supply strategy through rough-cut capacity planning (RCCP).
  • Lead the supply review process within the monthly S&OP cycle, presenting supply constraints, risks, and recommended mitigations to senior leadership.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for plant Operations teams on supply plan requirements, capacity utilization, and schedule feasibility.
  • Provide dotted-line oversight and direction to plant Master Schedulers, ensuring alignment between enterprise supply plans and facility-level Master Production Schedules (MPS).
  • Identify supply/demand imbalances and capacity constraints; develop and communicate resolution scenarios and trade-off analyses.
  • Collaborate with Demand Planning to ensure supply plans reflect the latest consensus forecast and support agreed service level targets.
  • Work with Procurement and Materials teams to align supply plans with material availability and lead time constraints.
  • Maintain and improve supply planning tools, capacity models, and ERP-based planning parameters, partner with the Planning Systems Manager on system enhancements.
  • Develop and monitor key supply planning KPIs including schedule attainment, capacity utilization, and inventory performance.
  • Lead a team of supply planners to optimize inventory levels, improve forecast accuracy, and ensure seamless product availability.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by supervisor.

Competencies:

  • Systems Thinking: Ability to understand and balance enterprise-level supply constraints across multiple facilities and product lines.
  • Collaboration & Communication: Strong interpersonal skills to align Operations, Procurement, and cross-functional teams on supply plan execution.
  • Analytical Thinking: Proficiency in capacity modeling, scenario analysis, and data-driven decision making.
  • Attention to Detail: Ability to manage and reconcile complex planning data across multiple horizons and facilities.
  • Leadership: Capability to influence and align dotted-line reports and operational stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Adaptability: Ability to respond quickly to supply disruptions, demand changes, and shifting operational priorities.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Operations, or a related field required.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in supply planning, master scheduling, or S&OP within a manufacturing environment.
  • Demonstrated experience with rough-cut capacity planning and MPS development.
  • Experience providing cross-functional or dotted-line leadership to scheduling or planning personnel preferred.
  • Proficiency with ERP systems required; INFOR/SyteLine experience highly preferred.
  • Experience with BI tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) required for KPI tracking and reporting.
  • APICS CPIM or CSCP certification preferred.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and capacity modeling tools.
  • ASCM CPIM certification preferred.
  • Demonstrated career ambition with a track record of growth and increasing responsibility; highly promotable with the potential to take on broader leadership roles within a fast-paced, high-growth organization

description:
At IEM, we’re not just building innovative electrical distribution systems, we’re shaping the future. IEM is dedicated to delivering world-class solutions for complex power needs. After 75 years, we continue to push the boundaries of what’s possible. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting out, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, grow, and make a lasting impact on industries that power the world’s most dynamic markets.

Position Summary:

The Supply Planning Manager is responsible for owning and driving the enterprise supply plan, including rough-cut capacity planning, as a core component of the company's Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) cycle. This role serves as the primary liaison between the supply chain organization and plant Operations, ensuring supply plans are feasible, executable, and aligned to customer demand.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and maintain the enterprise supply plan, translating the consensus demand plan into a feasible production and supply strategy through rough-cut capacity planning (RCCP).
  • Lead the supply review process within the monthly S&OP cycle, presenting supply constraints, risks, and recommended mitigations to senior leadership.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for plant Operations teams on supply plan requirements, capacity utilization, and schedule feasibility.
  • Provide dotted-line oversight and direction to plant Master Schedulers, ensuring alignment between enterprise supply plans and facility-level Master Production Schedules (MPS).
  • Identify supply/demand imbalances and capacity constraints; develop and communicate resolution scenarios and trade-off analyses.
  • Collaborate with Demand Planning to ensure supply plans reflect the latest consensus forecast and support agreed service level targets.
  • Work with Procurement and Materials teams to align supply plans with material availability and lead time constraints.
  • Maintain and improve supply planning tools, capacity models, and ERP-based planning parameters, partner with the Planning Systems Manager on system enhancements.
  • Develop and monitor key supply planning KPIs including schedule attainment, capacity utilization, and inventory performance.
  • Lead a team of supply planners to optimize inventory levels, improve forecast accuracy, and ensure seamless product availability.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by supervisor.

Competencies:

  • Systems Thinking: Ability to understand and balance enterprise-level supply constraints across multiple facilities and product lines.
  • Collaboration & Communication: Strong interpersonal skills to align Operations, Procurement, and cross-functional teams on supply plan execution.
  • Analytical Thinking: Proficiency in capacity modeling, scenario analysis, and data-driven decision making.
  • Attention to Detail: Ability to manage and reconcile complex planning data across multiple horizons and facilities.
  • Leadership: Capability to influence and align dotted-line reports and operational stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Adaptability: Ability to respond quickly to supply disruptions, demand changes, and shifting operational priorities.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Operations, or a related field required.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in supply planning, master scheduling, or S&OP within a manufacturing environment.
  • Demonstrated experience with rough-cut capacity planning and MPS development.
  • Experience providing cross-functional or dotted-line leadership to scheduling or planning personnel preferred.
  • Proficiency with ERP systems required; INFOR/SyteLine experience highly preferred.
  • Experience with BI tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) required for KPI tracking and reporting.
  • APICS CPIM or CSCP certification preferred.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and capacity modeling tools.
  • ASCM CPIM certification preferred.
  • Demonstrated career ambition with a track record of growth and increasing responsibility; highly promotable with the potential to take on broader leadership roles within a fast-paced, high-growth organization

PURPOSE OF POSITION

The Test Engineer is responsible for designing, developing, and executing test procedures for IEM products and components. This role ensures product quality and performance by analyzing test results, identifying issues, and leading extensive troubleshooting efforts, while supporting the development of robust test processes and driving continuous improvement across the test organization.



ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  • Design and develop test procedures and protocols.
  • Execute functional and electrical testing on products and components.
  • Collaborate with engineering and production teams to resolve product issues.
  • Analyze test data and identify trends, issues, and root causes.
  • Develop and improve testing methods and processes.
  • Support troubleshooting and failure analysis.
  • Ensure compliance with safety standards and testing procedures.
  • Maintain accurate test documentation and reports.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
  • Relay protection and trip function testing.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve wiring errors, component failures, and control logic issues.
  • Recommend upgrades or new test technologies to improve accuracy, capability, and efficiency.
  • FWT Support (Factory Witness Testing).

None.

  • Experience with automated test systems (LabVIEW, Python, NI, etc.)
  • Familiarity with PLC systems or embedded systems testing.
  • Background in high-reliability industries (aerospace, defense, medical devices).
  • Attention to detail and documentation accuracy.
  • Clear and professional communication.
  • Safety-conscious behavior with strict adherence to NFPA 70E and departmental safety standards.
  • Problem-solving and analytical thinking.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

This role leads daily test operations across all product lines, ensuring safe, efficient, and compliant execution of electrical testing. The Test Supervisor manages test technicians, drives throughput, and ensures product performance through troubleshooting and process control. This position also provides technical leadership by supporting test development, failure analysis, and continuous improvement across the test organization.

This position will be based temporarily in NE San Antonio while our new manufacturing plant is coming online. Our permanent location is approximately 25 minutes away at Brooks, 7515 Inner Circle Dr., San Antonio, 78235. The position is also 100% in-office and does not offer remote work.

title: Vice President, Solutions & Delivery
description:
At IEM, we’re not just building innovative electrical distribution systems, we’re shaping the future. IEM is dedicated to delivering world-class solutions for complex power needs. After 75 years, we continue to push the boundaries of what’s possible. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting out, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, grow, and make a lasting impact on industries that power the world’s most dynamic markets.

Location: US Remote

Reports To: Managing Director

Salary Range: $210,000-$220,000

Position Summary:

The Vice President, Solutions & Delivery is responsible for translating customer opportunities into technically sound, commercially competitive, and executable solutions, and then leading those solutions through successful project delivery. This role serves as the critical link between business development, customers, engineering, suppliers, and project execution. Working closely with the Managing Director and Director, Market Development, the VP, Solutions & Delivery will lead the development of customer solutions during the pre-sales phase, including technical definition, supplier engagement, cost development, pricing support, schedule development, and execution planning. Following contract award, the role assumes overall responsibility for delivery, ensuring that projects are executed safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with customer commitments. In the initial growth phase of the business, this will be a highly hands-on leadership role, personally leading key projects and supplier relationships while establishing the processes, partnerships, and delivery organization required to support future growth.

Key Responsibilities:

Solutions & Pre-Sales

  • Partner with the Managing Director and Director, Market Development to evaluate and develop qualified customer opportunities.
  • Lead the development of customer-specific technical and commercial solutions, particularly for EPCs, utilities, data centers, industrial customers, and other critical-power applications.
  • Translate customer requirements, specifications, and project constraints into an executable solution.
  • Develop project cost models and provide accurate cost inputs to support commercial proposals.
  • Engage suppliers and manufacturing partners to obtain competitive pricing, technical information, lead times, and commercial terms.
  • Develop preliminary project schedules, execution strategies, scopes of supply, and delivery assumptions.
  • Identify technical, commercial, schedule, and supply-chain risks before commitments are made to customers.
  • Participate in customer and EPC meetings as the company's solutions and delivery authority, supporting the commercial team through technical clarification, proposal development, and contract negotiations.
  • Ensure that what is proposed and sold can be successfully delivered at the expected cost, schedule, quality, and margin.

Project & Delivery Leadership

  • Assume overall delivery responsibility following contract award and provide continuity from proposal through execution.
  • Lead projects from contract handover through engineering, procurement, manufacturing, logistics, installation, commissioning, and customer acceptance.
  • Establish project budgets, schedules, milestones, reporting requirements, and risk registers.
  • Maintain accountability for project cost, schedule, quality, contractual scope, and overall delivery performance.
  • Manage changes in scope and ensure commercial impacts are identified and communicated appropriately.
  • Coordinate internal resources, customers, suppliers, contractors, and manufacturing partners throughout execution.
  • Provide clear project reporting and escalation to the Managing Director.
  • Lead resolution of delivery challenges while maintaining strong customer relationships.
  • Capture lessons learned and continuously improve estimating and execution based on actual project performance.

Supply Chain & Procurement

  • Own and develop the supply-chain strategy supporting the U.S. business.
  • Identify, qualify, negotiate with, and manage strategic suppliers and subcontractors.
  • Develop a competitive and reliable supplier network capable of supporting the company's growth.
  • Validate supplier pricing and continually identify opportunities to improve cost, lead time, quality, and commercial terms.
  • Manage critical procurement activities and supplier performance throughout project execution.
  • Develop appropriate sourcing strategies balancing domestic and international supply.
  • Work closely with manufacturing and engineering partners to ensure equipment and components meet project requirements.

COMPETENCIES:

  • Equally comfortable sitting across the table from an EPC or customer during the development of a multimillion-dollar opportunity as negotiating with a supplier, reviewing a project cost model, resolving an execution problem, or leading a project meeting.
  • Combines commercial awareness, technical understanding, supply-chain capability, and strong project execution experience.
  • Strong customer-facing communication and presentation skills.
  • Ability to operate effectively in an entrepreneurial environment with limited initial infrastructure.
  • Willingness to remain hands-on while simultaneously building the systems and organization required for growth.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Electrical or Mechanical preferred) or related technical field; MBA a plus.
  • 10+ years of experience in solutions engineering, project delivery, or program management for complex engineered equipment, electrical infrastructure, energy, or industrial capital projects.
  • Demonstrated project leadership across engineering, procurement, manufacturing, construction/installation, and commissioning.
  • Strong understanding of project costing, estimating, margin, cash flow, and commercial risk.
  • Experience developing and managing suppliers, subcontractors, and supply-chain strategy.
  • Experience working with EPCs, utilities, data centers, industrial customers, or other sophisticated capital-project customers.

description:

Position Summary:

IEM is currently seeking a Warehouse Supervisor for our Jacksonville, FL and will report into the Materials Manager.

This role plans, organizes, and oversees the shipping and receiving of parts and supplies used to assemble switchgear and related electrical equipment. The Warehouse Supervisor maintains accurate inventory through cycle counts and the annual physical inventory, and prior experience in an industrial manufacturing environment is required.

Please note: This position requires 100% in-office presence in our Jacksonville, FL offices and does not offer remote work.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Plan and coordinate work, and train, motivate, and monitor the team members who verify and keep records on incoming and outgoing shipments and prepare items for shipment
  • Review shipping notices, bills of lading, invoices, orders, and other records to set shipping priorities, work assignments, and shipping methods needed to meet shipping and receiving schedules, using knowledge of shipping procedures, routes, and rates
  • Oversee incoming and outgoing receiving and shipping activities to ensure accuracy, completeness, and condition of shipments as well as inventory accuracy
  • Maintain inventory of shipping materials and supplies
  • Inspect material handling equipment for defects and coordinate repairs
  • Direct movement of shipments from the shipping and receiving area to storage work areas
  • Assist team members with shipping and receiving activities as needed
  • Adhere to established safety guidelines
  • Directly supervise the Material Control Attendant
  • The candidate will be expected to perform additional duties as assigned to support the team and organization

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or GED required
  • At least 5 years of experience in warehousing, receiving, inventory control, or materials management within an industrial manufacturing environment, including 2 years of supervisory experience
  • Demonstrated competencies in technical capability, leadership, ethical conduct, performance management, communication, teamwork, and financial management
  • Demonstrated career ambition with a track record of growth and increasing responsibility; highly promotable with the potential to take on broader leadership roles within a fast-paced, high-growth organization

Physical Requirements:

This role is physically active, requiring standing and walking for about 75% of the shift and sitting for the remainder. Employees must be able to lift up to 50 lbs on a continuous basis, and to bend, squat, and climb as needed. The role also requires extended close work on a computer screen and the ability to see small or detailed items, along with the ability to interpret information and manage multiple tasks at once. Work takes place in both a climate-controlled office and a shop or warehouse area that is not climate-controlled, with exposure to heat, cold, moisture, noise, dust, and fumes.

Compensation actually offered for this role will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate's geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors. A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to the full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the level and position offered.

description:

Position Summary

The Workplace Coordinator is responsible for ensuring a positive and productive work environment at the San Antonio, TX IEM office. This person will be the first face visitors and employees see when they walk into IEM. They have an important job of making a great first impression and answering and directing inquiries. In addition, they will support the rollout of workplace programs and initiatives and help oversee day-to-day operations, including ad hoc administrative needs. The Workplace Coordinator partners closely with vendors and internal teams and helps maintain a space that reflects the company’s culture while supporting ongoing business growth.

Location

This will be a 100% onsite role working at IEM in San Antonio, TX. There will be no regular travel but may have opportunities to travel for IEM site visits, training and/or conferences.

Ideal Candidate Profile (Optional)

The ideal candidate is customer-focused, organized, and adaptable, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. This person is approachable, resourceful, and comfortable supporting both employee experience and operational needs. Experience with tools such as Microsoft Office Suite, SharePoint, and Verkada is a plus.

Key Responsibilities

Front Desk and Reception Duties

  • Greet, welcome and direct on-site visitors in a friendly and professional manner
  • Monitor visitor management system and issue visitor badges
  • Answer intercom, phone and in-person inquiries, providing general information to guests and employees
  • Receive mail and packages and assist with distribution
  • Perform administrative tasks such as mailing, data entry, printing badges, etc.

Office Operations

  • Maintain a safe, clean, and organized office environment
  • Order and manage office and break room supplies
  • Assist with updating workplace documents, policies and procedures
  • Partner with vendors and internal teams to ensure a seamless employee experience

Event Planning and Employee Engagement

  • Help organize and execute office-wide onsite events, special meetings and VIP visits
  • Collect feedback and data from employees to support continuous improvement efforts

In addition to the responsibilities listed above, the Workplace Coordinator may be asked, and must be able to successfully complete, the following responsibilities on an “as needed” basis:

  • Support larger workplace projects and space planning initiatives
  • Cross-collaborate with other teams and/or senior management
  • Assist the broader facilities team, from admin-type tasks to rolling up your sleeves and moving items that weigh up to 20lbs
  • Occasional extended hours may be required to support events or business needs
  • Flexible and adaptable team player who operates with agility and resourcefulness, and thrives in an often-changing environment. You will be operating with a start-up mindset and must be willing to help wherever needed - "not my job" is an unacceptable response

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Minimum of 3 years of receptionist/administrative assistant and/or front desk experience
  • Flexibility and customer focus are a must
  • Excellent organizational, written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to multitask and maintain attention to detail
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and ability to learn new systems quickly
  • Basic cash handling skills

Physical Demands

  • Activities:
    • Sitting – 80%
    • Walking/Standing – 20%
